text_simplified: Educational effort in raising children is an act of worship to Allah and a fulfillment of one's duty, along with certainty that Allah alone is the Guide. Parents have means mentioned in the Sunnah—encouragement, motivation, and deterrence—and they must continue to bear the trust (amanah). It is astonishing that a parent becomes anxious if his daughter refuses to go to school or her grades drop, yet never asks about her character, manners, or companions; he fears for her in this world but does not fear for her from the Fire. The author concludes with a prayer for the righteousness of intentions and offspring.

review_defects.why: The title drops 'صلاح' (righteousness) qualifying the Hereafter and softens 'حطام الدنيا' (worthless debris of this world) to merely 'Worldly Things'.
The Arabic attributes the amazement to 'the author' (المؤلف) and refers to 'one who' (ممن), but the English drops the author and inserts 'a parent' as the subject.
